The plan suits her: three walk-run mornings on her usual Mon/Wed/Sat, about 22, 22 and 25 minutes. That is roughly what 6.8 km over three walk-runs takes, so the volume and the longest session go up only a little, if at all. It keeps the same pattern and easy effort and adds a gentle calf-strength session on Friday, which fits her tight calves. Every non-running day is a rest day with her usual dog walk. Her calf tightness clears by the next morning, so it isn't an injury sign and doesn't need a referral. No must-never check is triggered. I took a point off for details the card doesn't support: "ten weeks" to the race (the card gives no current date) and a mention of shins she never raised. Also, "same walk-run pattern as last week" leaves the run and walk intervals vague for someone this new, so the days are a little less clear to run as written.

── NESSA'S WEEK ──
Nessa is 41 and new to running, aiming to run the whole Corrowmore Harvest 5K on 15 November without walking. Nessa walk-runs three mornings a week (Monday, Wednesday and Saturday) and walks the dog most days.
Recent weeks: none recorded.
This week: 6.8 km over 3 runs.
Body: "Calves tight the day after each run, gone by the next morning."
Feeling: "Proud I started."
Asks: "I want to be ready for the 5K in November. Should I run every day next week to get there faster?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Nessa: Great first week: three runs, no pain. …
Answers: (1) No, keep to three runs a week. Running every day would add far more load than your calves and shins are ready for, and your calves are already tight the day after each run. (2) You get fitter during the rest between runs, not during the runs themselves. Ten weeks is enough time to build up to running the whole 5K if you stay consistent with Monday, Wednesday and Saturday and don't get injured.
Next week:
Mon: easy, 22 min, same walk-run pattern as last week with a few minutes of walking at…
Tue: rest, no run. Dog walk as usual. Your calves adapt on days without running.
Wed: easy, 22 min, same pattern and same easy effort as Monday. Repeating the session…
Thu: rest, no run. Dog walk as usual. This gives your calves a day to recover before…
Fri: other, 15 min, gentle bodyweight strength: 2 sets of 10 calf raises, squats and…
Sat: easy, 25 min, same walk-run pattern and easy effort, your longest session so far…
Sun: rest, no run. Dog walk as usual. This ends the week fresh for the next step up.
